themes.mechanism: Two axes: `data-theme` (mode: dark/light, 'system' follows the OS) and `data-palette` (signal hue: tangerine/bubblegum/limeade/crayon, default tangerine) on <html>, both resolved in JS (src/lib/theme.ts) and painted flash-free by a boot script in index.html. The Tailwind semantic colors read CSS variables, so every mode x palette combo flows from one token vocabulary. COLOR-AS-ACCENT doctrine (2026-07-17): the neutral canvas is SHARED by every palette — palette blocks in src/index.css redefine only the accent family (--accent/--accent-ink/--on-accent), the meter, the --row-sel signal wash, and (where the signal collides with deletes) danger. Bevels/glow/motion inherit; the LED glow auto-follows via var(--accent-ink).

tangerine.feel: default; one juicy orange does all the talking, sunshine meter (#ffce33 / #b98600)

bubblegum.feel: hot magenta record-light, aqua meter (#2ee6c8 / #0d9488); danger shifts to plain red (#ff5c5c dark / #b91c1c light) so deletes never read as the pink signal

limeade.feel: lime on dark deepened to emerald in light for AA on white; violet meter (#b497ff / #7c58e8) as the wink

crayon.feel: cobalt signal, green meter (#3ddc74 / #1e9e4e); quietest chrome, the crayon-box note data carries the playfulness. The one palette where --on-accent diverges from --on-bright: the light cobalt fill carries white text

dark.displayName: The Listening Station, frosted (near-black canvas with an ambient signal bloom; workspace columns float as translucent blurred glass panes; color as accent)

light.displayName: White Glass (pale grey canvas with the ambient bloom; white 62% blurred panes; color only as accent)

rules: Accent-not-canvas (glass edition, 2026-09-05): panes are neutral glass in both modes. Color arrives only as the signal, the meter, the note data, the --row-sel wash on the selected row, and the ambient bloom behind the panes / the glow beneath the transport well (--ambient, .well-glow — both read the signal hue). A pane's own fill never carries a hue.

Frosted glass (2026-09-05): .glass = translucent panel fill + 28px backdrop blur + hairline ring (--glass-ring) + top highlight (--glass-hi) + deep soft shadow (--glass-shadow), 18px radius, 12px gutters. .glass-pop is the denser variant for menus/modals. panel/raised/inset/note are alpha washes (full colour strings), so nested surfaces stay translucent. Only a pane, menu or modal floats — never a card inside a pane; at most four panes on screen.

Two signals: `--accent` is the bright signal for FILLS/graphics (Play, spines, dots, progress); `--accent-ink` is the AA-safe variant for TEXT/LED/links/focus. Identical in dark, divergent in light (a fill-strength signal fails AA as text on white).

`--on-bright` is the text that sits ON a data-hue fill (timecode labels): dark in both themes. `--on-accent` is the text on the SIGNAL fill (Play, sign-in, copy): = on-bright everywhere except Crayon light, where the cobalt fill carries white text.
Note/tag/element hues stay raw as FILLS; used as TEXT or a 1px border on the white page they are mixed toward ink for AA (src/lib/noteColors.ts `hueText`).
Every light pair is WCAG AA verified: body/muted/placeholder/accent-ink >= 4.5:1, non-text graphics >= 3:1.

The White-Sheet Rule (2026-07-17, supersedes White-Page + Dark-Masthead): light is one clean white sheet INCLUDING the global header — the `.chrome-dark` dark-masthead zone was retired with the tinted chrome when the user chose color-as-accent-only. The LED glow is dropped in light (a glow is a dark-screen affordance).

display.purpose: The editable track title; the largest prose on screen. A tool, so it never shouts (<=1.125rem).

body.purpose: Note content and general UI copy; IBM Plex Sans (humanist-technical), ~65-75ch measure.

label.purpose: Panel title bars, badges, micro-controls. Monospace, uppercase, +0.2em.

mono.purpose: The transport/header clock and timecode tags. Signal-colored, tabular, glowing in dark.

shadows.name: inset-bevel
shadows.purpose: Recessed screens only: LED readouts, the meter well, inputs, the editor canvas.

shadows.name: raised-bevel
shadows.purpose: The primary Play button only. A hint of a physical key, never a gel button.

shadows.name: glass-shadow
shadows.purpose: The pane (.glass) and floating menus/modals (.glass-pop) — the only outer shadow in the system.

shadows.name: well-glow
shadows.purpose: The transport well throws a faint signal-coloured glow downward — the lit console under the recorder.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/active feedback on controls. Quiet and immediate.

motion.name: seg-flicker
motion.purpose: Segmented LED meter shimmer; staggered per segment to read like a VU meter.

components.name: btn-primary
components.description: The one filled key: signal pill, on-accent bold sans, raised bevel; brightens on hover. Play, Start mapping, Copy hand-in link.

components.name: btn-ghost
components.description: The workhorse: hairline outline, muted uppercase mono label; hover lifts text and border.

components.name: btn-signal
components.description: Signal outline: 10% accent fill, 70% accent border, accent mono label; the primary creative action beside a primary.

components.name: btn-icon
components.description: Ghost icon button, 26px in panes (32px round = btn-icon-lg in the masthead / video overlay). Hover = raised wash; active = 10% signal wash.

components.name: chip
components.description: Data pill on a 14% tint of --hue (hex passed inline; text via hueText). chip-outline = ring, no fill; chip-time = the timecode.

components.name: seg
components.description: Segmented control: a 10px inset well with 22px items; the active item sits on the raised wash in signal ink.

components.name: field
components.description: Inset well input: inset fill, hairline, 8px corners, inset bevel; focus swaps the border to the signal.

components.name: switch
components.description: One-size toggle (18x32): inset track, muted knob; on = 30% signal track, signal knob.

components.name: pop
components.description: Floating menu: dense glass (78% ink, 22px blur, hairline ring, pane shadow), 14px corners. Popover.tsx applies it.
components.css: .pop{overflow:hidden;border-radius:14px;background:rgb(26 26 30/.78);backdrop-filter:blur(22px) saturate(160%);border:1px solid rgb(255 255 255/.08);box-shadow:0 30px 70px -18px rgb(0 0 0/.65),0 2px 6px rgb(0 0 0/.35),inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255/.06)}

components.name: well
components.description: The transport console: inset fill, 14px corners, a faint signal glow beneath.

components.name: tile
components.description: Flat wash card for grids: panel fill, glass ring, 14px corners; hover = raised wash + stronger ring. No shadow, no lift.

components.name: strip
components.description: A 3% frosted band inside a pane: title bars, tool strips, table heads.

components.name: empty
components.description: Empty state: inset box, 14px corners, centred muted copy. Never a dashed outline.

components.name: led-readout
components.description: The transport/header clock: signal mono with a soft glow in dark, tabular figures.

components.name: title-bar
components.description: The frosted strip atop every pane: 40px, 3% wash, 70% hairline below, muted mono caps label.

narrative.overview: Sound Annotator is built like an audio analysis bench, not a web app. The stage is a deep neutral — near-black in dark, a pale grey in light — carrying a soft ambient bloom of the signal hue, and every workspace column floats on it as a pane of frosted glass (translucent, blurred, hairline-ringed, 18px corners). Everything still reads like instrument output: timecodes and counts are monospace, the transport is a recessed well with an LED clock, panels wear frosted title strips. It is dense by intent, optimized for a teacher who returns daily and knows it cold. Color is accent, never canvas: one playful selectable signal hue (Tangerine default) means 'now', a meter hue supports it, and the crayon-box note palette encodes identity — always paired with a timecode label so meaning survives a projector or a colorblind viewer.
keyCharacteristics: A deep neutral canvas (near-black dark / pale grey light) with an ambient bloom of the signal hue; workspace columns float on it as frosted-glass panes (.glass): translucent fill, 28px backdrop blur, hairline ring, top highlight, deep soft shadow, 18px corners, 12px gutters.
Color only as accent: one signal hue meaning 'now', a meter hue, and the crayon-box note data. Panes never take a tint; only the canvas glows.
Monospace tabular numerics for every timecode, count, and micro-label.
Soft corners (chips 6px / controls 8px / grouped 10px / wells + tiles + menus 14px / panes 18px / modals 24px); data chips are pills; Play and the transport steps are round.

One component vocabulary in src/index.css (@layer components): btn-ghost / btn-signal / btn-primary / btn-icon(-lg), chip (+outline/neutral/signal/time, hue via --hue), seg/seg-item, field, switch, pop/pop-row, well, strip, tile, empty. Nothing is hand-rolled.
Secondary controls hidden at rest, revealed on hover or focus.

rules.name: The Accent-Not-Canvas Rule (glass edition)
rules.body: Panes are neutral glass in both modes. Color arrives only as the signal, the meter, the note data, the --row-sel wash on the selected row, and the ambient bloom behind the panes / the glow beneath the transport well. A pane's own fill never carries a hue.

rules.name: The One-Float Rule
rules.body: Only a pane, a menu (.pop) or a modal (.glass-pop) floats and casts the glass shadow. Inside a pane, separate surfaces with the wash ramp (panel -> raised / inset) or a hairline; never nest a shadowed card inside a pane. Tiles in a grid are flat wash cards with no shadow and no hover lift. A screen has at most four panes.

rules.name: The Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Every control is a class from the component layer plus, at most, a width, a hover colour and `press`. A bespoke `rounded border border-line px-3 ...` string at a call site is a bug. Popover.tsx applies .pop itself.

rules.name: The One-Chip Rule
rules.body: A tag, section name, timecode or status reads as the same pill wherever it appears: .chip on a 14% tint of --hue (text via hueText for AA), .chip-outline for chips that are controls or mark a note's kind, .chip-time for timecodes.

rules.name: The Signal-Is-Now Rule
rules.body: The active palette's signal color means the present moment or the primary action, nothing else. It is forbidden as a decorative fill. If more than roughly 10% of a screen is the signal color, something non-temporal has stolen it.

rules.name: The Color-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Hue only ever encodes identity (which note), never emotion or hierarchy. Any color-coded element must also carry a text label (timecode), so it reads correctly on a dim projector and for colorblind users.

rules.name: The Bevel-Restraint Rule
rules.body: Bevels are 1px lighting hints on interactive controls only: the inset bevel on fields and readouts, the raised bevel on btn-primary. Textures, gloss and faux-material finishes are forbidden; the backdrop blur is the only material effect.

dos: Float the workspace columns as .glass panes; build depth inside a pane from the wash ramp and hairlines.
Build every control from the vocabulary classes; compose with `press`.
Keep numerics monospace and tabular: timecodes, counts, durations.
Keep the panes neutral glass; reserve the signal for 'now', the primary action and the ambient bloom.
Pair every color-coded chip with its text label; route chip text through hueText.
Hide secondary controls until hover/focus; let the resting UI stay calm.
donts: Don't ship a grid of small shadowed cards, an indigo accent, or evenly padded 'friendly SaaS' whitespace. Glass panes are columns, not cards; tiles never float.
Don't drift into gray-on-gray toolbars, competing controls, data-grid busyness. Density is welcome; clutter is not.
Don't use retro skeuomorphism: fake textures, glossy bevels, brushed metal. Bevels stay 1px and only on controls.
Don't let color carry meaning alone, and don't add a third typeface.
Don't introduce a second solid-signal control next to Play, tint a pane's own fill with the signal beyond --row-sel, nest a shadowed card inside a pane, or hand-roll a button/chip/field.
